guide.p: Part 1 nearly always includes a name spelt letter by letter, a number and a date or time. These are the easiest marks in the test — and the easiest to lose through one wrong letter.

bullets: Practise the letters that are easy to confuse: A/E/I, G/J, B/V/P, M/N, S/F, Q/U, W/double U.
'Double' means two of the same: 'double L' = LL, 'double seven' = 77.
Names are often corrected: 'Smith — no, Smyth, with a Y'.
Thirteen/thirty, fourteen/forty, fifteen/fifty, etc.: the stress is at the end in '-teen' (thir-TEEN) and at the start in '-ty' (THIR-ty). Speakers sometimes clarify: 'three-oh, not one-three'.
Prices: '£12.50' may be said 'twelve fifty' or 'twelve pounds fifty'.
You can write dates in any clear form: 3 May, May 3, 3rd May.
If the form already shows the month, write only the day.
UK postcodes mix letters and numbers, for example 'BS8 1TH'. Copy the exact order.
Reference numbers often have a correction or repeated digits.

guide.tip: Write letters in capitals while you listen. Lower-case letters like 'a' and 'd' are easy to misread later.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: Westfield Health Centre, registration desk. Can I take your surname, please?

script.speaker: woman
script.text: Thank you. And your date of birth?

script.speaker: man
script.text: The thirteenth of March, nineteen ninety-four. Sorry, I mean the thirtieth. Three-oh, not one-three.

script.speaker: woman
script.text: No problem. And a contact number?

script.speaker: man
script.text: It's oh-seven-seven-one-four, double five, two, eight, nine, six.

script.speaker: man
script.text: L-S-six, four-G-W. And my first appointment is at quarter to eleven, if you need that too.

explain.2: He corrects himself: 'Sorry, I mean the thirtieth. Three-oh, not one-three.'
explain.3: 'oh-seven-seven-one-four, double five, two, eight, nine, six' = 07714 552896.
